title.en: Tell the story at the reunion
title.es: Contar la anécdota en la reunión familiar

es: Contar una anécdota familiar completa (escena y hábito pasado, hecho, giro y desenlace) y responder con naturalidad a las preguntas del público.

teaching.en: At every family reunion, my uncle would tell the same story about his first car.
teaching.es: En cada reunión familiar, mi tío contaba la misma historia sobre su primer coche.
teaching.explanationEs: Would + verbo abre la anécdota con un hábito del pasado.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase abre la anécdota con un hábito del pasado?

choices.text: At every reunion, my uncle tells the same story now.
At every reunion, my uncle would tell the same story.
At every reunion, my uncle has told the same story.

feedback.es: Would + verbo describe una acción habitual del pasado. Las otras dos hablan del presente o de un hecho perfecto sin hábito.

hint.es: Un hábito del pasado usa would + verbo base.

prompt.es: Completa: «Cuando llegó la tarta, mi tía llevaba una hora esperando.»

feedback.es: La espera duró hasta un momento pasado: past perfect continuous, had been waiting.

hint.es: Es el auxiliar del past perfect continuous.

origin.text: By the time the cake arrived, my aunt ___ been waiting for an hour.

prompt.es: Ordena la pregunta del público: «¿De verdad te comiste toda la tarta?»

answer.text: Did you really eat the whole cake?

feedback.es: Did va con el verbo en forma base (eat) y really va entre el sujeto y el verbo.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué recursos usa el hablante para empezar la historia.

choices.text: A past habit and a scene.

feedback.es: Empieza con un hábito del pasado (would take us fishing) y una escena con olor y fondo (the air smelled of pine). No hay giro ni pregunta todavía.

origin.audio: When I was a child, my grandfather would take us fishing every summer. The river was quiet, and the air smelled of pine.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada recurso con su papel en la anécdota.

pairs.es: Escena con un detalle del olfato

feedback.es: Cada recurso cumple un papel: fragmentos para el final, eco para reaccionar, little did I know para anticipar y un detalle de olfato para la escena.

pairs.es: Escena con un detalle del olfato

prompt.es: Completa: hábito (would), fondo anterior y acción a punto de ocurrir.

feedback.es: Would abre el hábito, had been planning da el fondo anterior y was about to marca la acción a punto de ocurrir.

sentences: At every reunion, my uncle ___ tell the same story.
By then, Grandma ___ been planning the prank for weeks.
I was ___ to cut the cake when the lights went out.

prompt.es: Cuenta la anécdota (unas 140 palabras) y responde a las dos preguntas del público.

answer.text:
Every summer, the whole family used to meet at my grandmother's house. The kitchen smelled of coffee, and the relatives were all talking at once. My uncle Tom would always tell the same story about his first car. That year, he was about to start it again when a stranger walked into the garden. Nobody recognised him. Silence. Then my grandmother laughed and opened her arms. "It's Leo!" she said. He had been travelling for ten years, and nobody had known where he was. Little did we know that he would stay with us for the whole summer.
Did you recognise him? No, I didn't. I thought he was a neighbour.
What did your uncle say? Fair enough, he said. Tonight, for once, we'll hear a new story.
accepted:
Every summer, the whole family used to meet at my grandmother's house. The kitchen smelled of coffee, and the relatives were all talking at once. My uncle Tom would always tell the same story about his first car. That year, he was about to start it again when a stranger walked into the garden. Nobody recognised him. Silence. Then my grandmother laughed and opened her arms. "It's Leo!" she said. He had been travelling for ten years, and nobody had known where he was. Little did we know that he would stay with us for the whole summer.
Did you recognise him? No, I didn't. I thought he was a neighbour.
What did your uncle say? Fair enough, he said. Tonight, for once, we'll hear a new story.

When I was a child, we would all meet at my grandmother's house on Sundays. The kitchen smelled of bread, and the relatives were all laughing in the garden. My uncle Tom used to tell the same story about his first car. One Sunday, he was about to begin when a tall man walked into the garden. Nobody knew him. Silence. Then my grandmother smiled and opened her arms. "It's Leo," she said. He had been living abroad for ten years, and nobody had heard from him. Little did I know that he would become my best friend.
Did you know him? No, I didn't. I thought he was a friend of my uncle.
What did your uncle say? Honestly, he said nothing. He just hugged him.

feedback.es: Una buena versión abre con hábito o escena, rompe con un hecho o was about to, da el giro con had been o Little did we know y responde a las preguntas del público con respuestas cortas.

origin.text: Situación: reunión familiar en casa de tu abuela. Cada verano el tío Tom contaba la misma historia del coche. Un año, iba a empezar cuando entró un desconocido en el jardín: era el primo Leo, al que nadie veía desde hacía diez años. Cuenta la anécdota (unas 140 palabras) con: un hábito o escena del pasado (used to / would), un hecho con was about to, un giro con had been o Little did we know y un final corto. Después responde a dos preguntas del público: «Did you recognise him?» y «What did your uncle say?».

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cuántas veces había oído la historia el hablante a los doce años.

feedback.es: «By the time I was twelve, I had heard it twenty times»: el past perfect fija la cifra anterior a los doce años.

origin.audio: At every reunion, my uncle would tell the story about his first car. By the time I was twelve, I had heard it twenty times. Then, last summer, he forgot the ending, and the whole family laughed.

prompt.es: Completa anteposición, cabeza y desenlace con little.

feedback.es: Con nombre la anteposición invierte (came my grandmother); la cabeza necesita el pronombre (she's); little pide inversión con did.

sentences: Into the kitchen ___ my grandmother, carrying a big cake.
Little ___ we know that he would stay.

prompt.es: ¿Qué respuesta del público muestra interés con un eco?

choices.text: Did she? How did she keep it secret?
Had she? How did she keep it secret?
Has she? How did she keep it secret?

feedback.es: La frase original usa had planned (had): el eco correcto es Had she?, que repite el auxiliar, y luego una pregunta.

origin.text: Ana: "Grandma had been planning the prank for weeks."

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase muestra el miedo en vez de nombrarlo?

choices.text: He was very afraid of the dog.
His hands were shaking, and he hid behind the door.

feedback.es: Las manos que tiemblan y esconderse detrás de la puerta son acciones que el lector ve. Las otras dos nombran la emoción.

prompt.es: Escucha la historia y ordena: ¿qué pasó en primer lugar?

feedback.es: «Two weeks earlier, my grandmother had bought the bread» es lo más antiguo; después estuvo horneando y por último llegó la familia.

origin.audio: The prank was a success. Two weeks earlier, my grandmother had bought the bread. By the time we arrived, she had been baking for three hours.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Nunca había visto a mi tío tan callado.»

answer.text: Never had I seen my uncle so quiet

feedback.es: Never al inicio pide inversión: never + auxiliar + sujeto (had I seen).
